COMMITTEE ON HOUSING AND BUILDINGS 6 New York City is facing its worst affordability crisis and decades driven in large part by housing costs. As the cost of rent and housing skyrocket, working- and middle-class New Yorkers who have been here for generations who have helped to build our city are struggling to remain in their homes. Last week, we had a hearing on the City's Housing and Vacancy Survey. The most recent findings highlight a vacancy rate of 1.4 percent, the lowest on record. The findings also highlight what I understand and what we can understand as a hypergentrification of New York City, one like we've never seen before with working-class and low-income families leaving our city while being replaced by higher-income households earning over 200,000 dollars per year. In my District, 61 percent of renters are rent-burdened meaning that they're paying more than 30 percent of their monthly income in rent. The housing stock is also falling apart. More than 55 of every 100 units in my District has a code violation and, across the city, CSS, Community Service Society, estimates that over 100,000 families in 10,000 buildings are living with multiple conditions that are hazardous to their health and safety.
